Due to the fact that the joint Croatian and Muslim forces had planned to cut off the western part of Republika Srpska from its eastern part through Doboj, the witness spoke to General Talic and informed him about those intentions on the part of Muslim and Croatian militaries. First he spoke to General Talic, and then he spoke about the same matter to General Mladic and President Karadzic. After that, a decision was made to embark on the breakthrough of the corridor. Witness Milivoje Simic was present when General Mladic visited Doboj. That happened on three or four occasions. The last time when General Mladic was in Doboj, there was a meeting which was attended by the witness, as well as Milan Martic, Momir Talic, and General Ratko Mladic. On that occasion, General Mladic referred to the killings of Muslims from Srebrenica. He said that that should not have happened and also that somebody had done it unbeknownst to him and without his approval. Your Honour, with your permission, I would like to ask the witness a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Lukic. MR. S. LUKIC: Thank you. Could we have paragraph 28 on English version. It's page 5 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, in your statement, in paragraph 28, you stated that General Mladic came to Doboj on three or four occasions. Did you see him every time or did you attend those meetings every time?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: When the offensive, i.e., Operation Corridor started, General Mladic visited the corps command, i.e., General Talic, on three or four occasions. I met with him on three occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What did the general have to tell you during those meetings?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Every time General Mladic came to Doboj, we had meetings, and those meetings were really very brief. Every time he alerted us to the fact that we should comply with the law during war operations, that we should apply the provisions of the rules of war. He spoke to us about our treatment of prisoners of war, selective targeting in order to minimise the number of civilian casualties. He also told us that we should be particularly mindful of women and children, and, finely, that we should try and preserve the already existing settlements. The ongoing theme was compliance with the Geneva Conventions, rights of civilians and prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. That will be all for the time being. MR. S. LUKIC: [Previous translation continues] ... for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Lukic. One very short question, Witness, this meeting where you say in paragraph 28 that General Mladic was talking about the events following the fall of Srebrenica, do you know on what date General Mladic spoke those words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember the date. It was at the beginning of August 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember that, but I really wouldn't be able to give you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Mr. Simic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You find Mr. Traldi to your right. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, how long have you known General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I first met him on 26th of May, 1992, in Banja Luka. He was the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you begin your statement by describing your service in Doboj and then in Croatia. You were a JNA officer when you served in Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you continued to hold a post in what became the VJ during your service in the VRS up until 1994; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, as a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were paid by the VJ; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Eventually through the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you retired in 1994; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: In 1994 or, rather, in 1995. In 1995, I was already retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to ask now some questions about Operational Group Doboj. Now, first, during your time as commander of Operational Group Doboj, who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: My immediate superior was the commander of the 1st Corps, General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And during the time that you served in Doboj, the Chamber's received evidence that non-Serbs from Prijedor and Bosanski Novi were transported out of Serb territory via Doboj. As OG Doboj commander, you were aware of these large groups of people being transported through your area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I personally didn't know that, but I suppose that General Talic did. Because the area of responsibility was under the corps command. I was a unit and an officer subordinated to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your understanding would be that as part of his job, that's information he would have to know; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence that one of those transports from Bosanski Novi had several thousand people on it, several hundred of whom were taken off the train in Doboj and sent back. Wouldn't you also have had to be aware of that since it was in your area of responsibility? And in case it refreshes your recollection, that was in June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: June 1992. I don't know what the date was exactly. Operation Corridor started. Everything that has to do with these transports, I was not informed about that. This was done by the services of the 1st Krajina Corps or, rather, the Doboj centre of security services. I personally did not take part. I was not informed. Quite simply, that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to Operation Corridor briefly. Now, during the summer of 1992 and particularly during Operation Corridor, there was 1st Krajina Corps forward command post in your area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That command post was first in Prnjavor and second in a place called Djuge [sic] Njive; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Duge Njive is where I was stationed, not Prnjavor. Never Prnjavor. Duge Njive, that's above Modrica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I understand and let me try to clarify the question. I wasn't asking where you were stationed, I was asking where the 1st Krajina Corps' forward command post was and there was such a forward command post in your area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: At Duge Njive, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And General Talic and General Kelecevic were also often present there; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Kovacevic? I don't know about that person. Kovacevic? What was his position? I don't know of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Perhaps my speed was off, sir --

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: What time was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Perhaps my speed was off. If you give me a moment, I'll re-ask the question slowly. General Talic and General Bosko Kelecevic were often present at that forward command post during the summer of 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you would meet them regularly because they were present in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, practically we were one command that was in charge of the operations because I had units, my units, that I resubordinated to the corps units in order to have this task accomplished from Doboj to Brod, to the Sava river.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when General Mladic visited, you've said you met with him, he would also visit that command post; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Duge Njive, yes. Duge Njive. That's where we were. That's where he saw us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it goes without saying, I suppose, but when you had a superior officer present in your area of responsibility, you'd obviously run any important decisions past them for their approval, consistent with the chain of command; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, in the chain of command, I was subordinated to General Talic, so everything that was done within the chain of command, what was received from the Main Staff he got that. He sent it down to me and I sent it down to my units. That's how it went.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, turning to the corridor operation, that was carried out pursuant to a directive, directive 1, issued by the Main Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a question about the purpose of that operation in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But first I'm go to ask Ms. Stewart to play a short video-clip. We will have to play it twice because it has not been pre-confirmed, and that's 65 ter 22338b.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] the second purpose of this operation is to open a corridor towards Serbia. In this way, we shall secure the area of the Krajinas. It is easier for me to say Krajinas than the Knin Krajina and Bosanska Krajina. Thus, we shall secure the necessary raw materials for industry to work, and above all, to procure medicines and other essentials for children and the infirm. The third aim of the operation is for us to link up with the East Bosnian Corps and in co-ordination with them, to penetrate to the borders of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and to join them to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: General Talic there states that among the purposes of the corridor operation is to link up the 1st Krajina Corps and the East Bosnia Corps, penetrate to the borders of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and join them to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Was that also how you understood the purposes of Operation Corridor?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I understood is that because Doboj was under siege, blocked from all sides by the Croat/Muslim forces. We just had the railroad going to Banja Luka as our only way out of there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender 65 ter 22338b.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the video receives number P7173.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7173 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the establishment of that corridor linking the eastern and western parts of -- of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, at the time you were aware that was one of the strategic objectives of the Bosnian Serb people that President Karadzic had set out at the 16th Assembly Session; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your Operational Group carried out operations including, Operation Corridor in furtherance of those strategic objectives; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Part of the operations group. Most of it was securing Doboj and the Serb villages. Only two of my brigade, two of my brigades of the Territorial Defence, with two ^ to 2500 soldiers were included in the operation at Doboj, Plemen, Derventa, Brod, within Tactical Group 3 that was commanded by Colonel Slavko Lisica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to make sure that the record is clear as to my question. Units within your operation group carried out operations including Operation Corridor in furtherance of the strategic objectives; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you've mentioned Tactical Group 3 under Colonel Lisica. In the summer of 1992 there were four tactical groups within Operational Group Doboj; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The commander of tactical group was --

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The zone of the corps, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The commander of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Slavko Lisica 3, 3. 1, Novica Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 4, Radmilo Zeljaja?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: His task was to prevent an attack from the Croat/Muslim forces from the direction of Gradacac, so that they would not hit us from the back or on the flanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, those three men were all VRS officers; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: At that time, yes, and they belonged to the units of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who was the commander of Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Tactical Group 2, it was Milan Martic. Within the operations of the corps, it was included in Tactical Group 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now he was included in Tactical Group 2. Was the commander of that group at some point actually Mile Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. Colonel Mile Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And which army was he in at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: At that moment, it was the Army of the Serb Krajina. I mean, Martic's police. That's what it was called at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the tactical groups included, along with VRS forces, forces from the police of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, forces from the Army of Republic of Serbian Krajina and RS MUP forces including forces from the Doboj CSB; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And during the course of the corridor operation, those forces were under the unified command of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, General Talic, the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I left one group out. There were also units fighting in Doboj and elsewhere in the Posavina corridor which had been trained, equipped and were paid by the Serbian DB; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 32067.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, do you remember units that were known as Red Berets being present in your zone of operations in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were in Doboj, but not at the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in Doboj, there's a payroll list for the Ministry of Interior Security Services Centre Doboj. We see, for instance, at number 1, a man named Radojica Bozovic. And you knew him, in fact, to be from Serbia, didn't you? Or when I say "from Serbia," I should say to be employed by the Serbian DB; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I met him, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And did you know that he was employed by the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I did know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were aware that his and other Red Berets units were active in your zone of operations; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, for a while. They just created difficulties for us. We got rid of them very quickly in an organised manner. We didn't need the likes of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours 32067 receives number P7174.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now one more point on your positions, sir. At one point, you became a member of the Doboj War Presidency; right.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32156.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in the top right corner of the page in B/C/S, we see an article entitled: "We all have a joint task." And at the top of the article, we see a reference to one of the people who's made it possible for the Serbian people in the Serbian municipality of Doboj to celebrate their first anniversary in a Serbian state, a Colonel Milivoje Simic. So this is an article about you; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I want to look at your response to the third question, and in the B/C/S it's the middle of the right column immediately below your picture, I believe. Above and below. And you note that: "I don't think that military and civilian tasks can be separated from each other in this war. We all have a joint task and that is how we are carrying [sic] out." And that reflects your understanding of the co-operation between the VRS and the Bosnian Serb civilian authorities at that time; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now at the end of the article you note that the corps commander for civilian sector had tasked you with directly helping local government organs. Now you're referring to the assistant commander for civilian affairs, Colonel Gojko Vujinovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Civilian, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd tender this interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 32156 receives number P7175.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. I'm still trying to find your last quote at the end of the article. Is this still on the page we have on our screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It -- it's not. Not in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yep, I see that it's on the -- apparently on the second page. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to turn now, sir, to some of the groups you describe in your statement as paramilitaries. You mention Slobodan Karagic's unit. Now, Mr. Karagic was a member of the special unit of CSB Doboj; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You mention Preda Kujundzic, in fact that was Predrag Kujundzic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he was also a worker for CSB Doboj; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32062.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an Official Note coming from the National Security Service Sector of CSB Banja Luka. And we see an information at the beginning that Predrag Kujundzic, a worker of the CSB Doboj, acquired for himself and his group, by means of loot, around 70 kilograms of gold in jewellery, that he had appropriated for himself a large quantity of foreign money. And that: "In the course of the cleansing of the village of Civcije, the municipality of Doboj, his group handed 350,000 German marks to him which he did not forward to the appropriate institutions." Were you aware that Mr. Kujundzic's group was involved in large-scale looting in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I didn't know about these details and these quantities, but I know what he was doing, and I cautioned Andrija Bjelosevic specifically at the centre in Doboj that he should take care of his men because people were complaining. They were not very selective. They were looting Serb houses and apartments just like Croat and Muslim ones. That I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kujundzic after the war was convicted of crimes in Bosnia committed against non-Serbs in the Doboj municipality in July 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we saw here a reference to the cleansing of the village of Civcije. You're aware, aren't you, that in the summer of 1992, Muslims from Civcije were taken away to detention facilities including a place called Percin's disco; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The Doboj Centre for Security Services was engaged in that. We were in our offensive at that point in time. We didn't deal with any of that. I was not informed to what degree but I just know that men from the village of Civcije as our civilian police or, rather, the centre of the security services, they barged in, they arrested the people from there, but where they took them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're ware that Muslim houses in Civcije and the mosque there were destroyed; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The mosque, yes. Serb houses were not. I mean, the houses were not. Because Serb refugees from elsewhere, from Ozren, et cetera later came to live in these houses, but the mosque had been destroyed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I tender 65 ter 32062, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I see that the title is not fully translated. It says: National Security Service Sector. But Banja Luka is not in the title in the English version, and you referred to it as under the title which we find in the B/C/S. Could you have the translation be verified. At the same time, Mr. Lukic, I'm looking at you, if that would be the only issue, then I would not, at this moment, deny admission, but it certainly should be checked. What you could do is to check it, whether everything else translated and if so we either leave it that's it -- on the record that the words "Banja Luka" are missing or you provide a new translation if there's more. MR. S. LUKIC: Thank you, Your Honour. We'll check it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number would be P7176.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence with the caveat as I expressed before. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You also refer in your statement to one paramilitary unit which you say was of considerable strength from Prnjavor. The commander of that unit was Veljko Milankovic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The Prnjavor Brigade participated in Operation Corridor, but Milankovic never came to Doboj. He was engaged on the axis starting with Modrica. I personally saw him in Duge Njive, which was the corps command post. He was in charge of a group, a paramilitary formation, that is, and together with the units it was engaged, but I don't know what its task was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that unit also committed crimes, including looting, during the summer of 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes. From what I could learn, the answer would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Milankovic, by the start of the corridor operation, was, in fact, a battalion commander in the 327th Motorised Brigade of the VRS, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. I know that he was more independent than a member of a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, can we have P3826.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an order signed by General Talic on the 5th of June, 1992. And we see at point 1 that a battalion from the Prnjavor Territorial Defence Command is being transferred to the Command of the 327th Motorised Brigade and fully incorporated into it, and that General Talic is appointing Lieutenant Veljko Milankovic as battalion commander. Does that refresh your recollection as to whether Milankovic was, during the corridor operations, a battalion commander in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether his unit was a battalion. It was a somewhat larger group, and they did whatever they wanted to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the stamp we see on this document, this is the Operational Group Doboj stamp; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Operational Group Doboj, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you explain for us the meaning of the symbol that we see in the centre of the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: These are four Ss. Those are usually the markings found on the Serbian coat of arms. The four Ss. I know that that was the name of this symbol.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And culturally, it's a Serb nationalist symbol; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What do the four Ss stand for? They're an abbreviation; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I really wouldn't be able to tell you. These are just the four Ss depicted on the Serbian flag and those who made stamps also incorporated them into the stamps, but I really wouldn't be in a position to tell you what that means.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were aware, you said a moment ago --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And now, Your Honour, I was about to turn to a slightly different topic. I saw one of the Judges might have had a question and so I was stopping to provide an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I didn't. I was just communicating with my colleague here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This document is, let me just have a look, is tendered, is admitted already. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned that you were aware that Milankovic's unit committed crimes including looting you were also aware of that during the summer of 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: As the operation progressed, he often went to Prnjavor which was his own area. He returned. He was subordinated to the corps command and he reported to General Kelecevic, Bosko Kelecevic, who was the Chief of Staff of the 1st Corps. Kelecevic commanded him, he gave him tasks, I can tell you that because I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play one more -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we receive an answer to the question. The question was whether you were aware of Milankovic's unit committing crimes, including looting, during the summer of 1992. Can you please answer whether you were aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew some things but not the details. I was not authorised to know any details. He was incorporated into the corps unit on the order of the corps commander. I did not receive reports from him. I had my own tasks. He didn't report to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that still does not exclude for the possibility that you know something about it. Witness, you'll hear me --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was aware of some things, but not of any details. Only the person to whom he reported was aware of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if you say, "Of some things," that would include criminal activities, including looting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, some of that, yes. When we spoke to Kelecevic, we learned that wherever he was with his group, there were problems, that those things should be presented, that he should be chased away. Such proposals were heard in conversations with Kelecevic and the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in fact, the Chamber has received evidence that Milankovic was - although posthumously - decorated by the 1st Krajina Corps command. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I really don't know that. I don't know that he was decorated, when and why. And where. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see we're close to time for the break. I'm about to turn to a slightly different matter and so I'd recommend that we take it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take the break now. Mr. Simic, we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back after -- yes, it's a bit confusing for you who is addressing because you hear it all through an interpreter but it's the Presiding Judge now who is speaking to you. We'll take a break, and we'll resume in 20 minutes. We'd then like to see you back. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom. Mr. Traldi, you have already any document on your mind which ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I hate to waste time. I am going to ask Ms. Stewart to play another clip and I suppose we could do the first run-through for CLSS ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's -- let's wait for a second so that gives the witness an opportunity to look at it twice, which ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, just to clarify what I said before the break, I'm actually going to stick to a very similar matter for one more clip and if I could ask Ms. Stewart to play 65 ter 22663a.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] Momcilo Krajisnik, master of arts, president of the national Assembly of Republika Srpska and candidate of the SDS for the member of the Presidency of the union addressed those gathered at the fifth anniversary of the renowned unit Vukovi sa Vucijaka. "You Vukovi sa Vucijaka who are present here today in civilian clothes rather than in uniforms, you belong to this area as much as you belong to people of Dalmatia, Lika, Western Slavonia, Posavina. Your war path is difficult but glorious. Since 1991, when you lit the torch of freedom defending the people of the Serbian Krajina, you went through all theatres of war and participated in many combats in Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Both your friends and enemies will remember your heroism. You and your legendary commander, Veljko Milankovic are history's favourites. I have no doubt ... I have no doubt that children in schools, and especially military school cadets, will ask themselves when studying about our combat - what were they like? What -- which formation did Vukovi sa Vucijaka belong to? The response will be: It was the unit every army in the world would be proud of. Your deeds are immortal because each of were worth two men. In other words, we can simply say: You belonged to the entire Serbian people."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I have just a couple of simple questions with you about that video. First, Mr. Krajisnik refers to the fifth anniversary of Milankovic's units, that places these remarks after the war; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: By that point, Milankovic's unit's involvement in the crimes that you mentioned, crimes including looting, was well-known, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I know something about that, but not everything. Like most of the people, so ... yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender that clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 22663a receives number P7177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7177 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, during the summer of 1992, you were also directly informed about crimes being committed by members of Serb forces in your area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No, not me directly. Perhaps General Talic. My main areas were Doboj and Teslic, and my two units were attached to the corps unit, but, as such, they were the responsibility of the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you've suggested that you had command over a limited number of the units within Operational Group Doboj a couple of times now. Was it that the 1st Krajina Corps Command, General Talic and General Kelecevic was exercising direct command --

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Wait for the end of the question. Was the 1st Krajina Corps exercising direct control over the other units within what was formally Operational Group Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, you said a moment ago you suggested you had two units which were attached to the corps unit. You testified earlier that Operational Group Doboj had four tactical groups. Those four tactical groups, they were under your command; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: No. Corps command had four tactical groups that were under its command. My two brigades were elements of TG3. Colonel Lisica was the commander. They were considered to be a corps unit participating in the breakthrough of the corridor. That would be that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going look at the two municipalities that you referred to a moment ago as your main area, Doboj and Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32065. And this will relate to Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see a communication from the Ministry of the Interior, Security Services Centre, Doboj. We see it comes from Chief Andrija Bjelosevic and we see the last of the addressees, the commander of the Operational Group Colonel Milivoje Simic. That's you; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And under the subject line we read: "We have been dissatisfied for quite a long time with the security situation in our region and especially in Doboj municipality. There is an increasing incidence of murder, looting, export of vehicles and Muslims and Ustashas departing for Serbia ..." Now, does that refresh your recollection as to whether you were directly informed of crimes being committed by members of Serb forces in your area of responsibility during 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: That was done by paramilitary formations and forces of the public security centre. There were some renegade groups there as well. They were not under anybody's command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm speaking. Could you please answer the question rather to elaborate on. The question was about whether you were directly informed about these crimes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi is asking this because he sees that you are one of the addressees and whereas this letter, this document, describes those crimes. So, therefore, he was seeking confirmation that you would be directly informed. But could you explain, considering this letter, why you say you were not directly informed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was on the 23rd of September, 1992. Perhaps that. In the month of September. That was almost the end of Operation Corridor. I was not in Doboj. He informed me about everything, but that was on the 23rd of September. He informed me about certain things that he was supposed to deal with. They were the ones who arrested people, brought them in, forwarded them for trials. The command did not have anything to do with that, as command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Two more questions about this document. At the end of the paragraph, Chief Bjelosevic refers to Muslims and Ustashas departing to Serbia. By Ustasha, he means ethnic Croats, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, second, they were leaving because of the crimes that he's describing, which were being perpetrated against them, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tendered 65 ter 32065.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 32065 receives number P7178.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7178 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask briefly now about one other municipality, Odzak. That was also part of this same corridor operation; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play a clip 65 ter 22338c.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're going to play it twice, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We are. And I apologise for not stating that explicitly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] was mainly inhabited by Croats, I say was, as this is now a ghost town. There are still fresh traces of fighting. But why was the war fought for this town? It's only now apparent that the local Croats had prepared to settle scores with their neighbours a long time before the conflict erupted. Immediately after the civil war began, strong Croatian forces were concentrated here. Serbs were brought from the neighbouring towns of Novi Grad, Modrica and Novo Selo. A really concentration camp was formed here on the football pitch, and all this in a place where people had once lived well and in prosperity in and from the old Yugoslavia. It is obvious that there was to desire here for peaceful life, on the contrary. "General Ratko Mladic: Since they didn't want this but instead attacked us, attempted to destroy and burn the Serbian population, you yourself can see how they fared. Here we are in a place where I found myself for the first time. This is an entire town where people prospered, where the former Yugoslavia gave them much more than all of us put together. I belonged to a category which some might say was privileged because I was an officer, and, of course, better paid. However, I could only dream of what people had here. The Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia gave everything to these people. They converted their houses into bunkers, shelters, underground casemates and torture Chambers for Serbs. "Reporter: It is down to these people that Odzak which they have made into a town of evil, today looks so sad and empty."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, we heard in that video Odzak describes as a ghost town and as looking sad and empty. Odzak was, as the reporter said, mainly inhabited by ethnic Croats before the war; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's correct, isn't it, that thousands of people fled after the VRS attacked it, leaving the town looking, as it was described there, sad and empty; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 22338c.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the video receives number P7179.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7179 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned General Mladic visited several times during the corridor operation. One of those was that he was in Duge Njive on 16th of July, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to turn away from that subject and turn to another of the municipalities you mentioned, Teslic. Now the Chamber has received evidence that you deployed some of your subordinates, including Captain Ljubisa Petricevic and Major Jovo Popovic to Teslic around the 1st of June, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar this event. Petricevic was chief of the Ministry of Defence in Doboj. This is civilian authority. He was not subordinated to me. I was not his superior. I could not give him orders, despite what it says in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall Ranko Sljuka, Zoran Sljuka, Dario Slavuljica, and Miroslav Pijunovic as having been among your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: They were not my subordinates, no. I don't know whose subordinates they were, but they were certainly not mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the next question I ask -- I'd suggest the witness be advised of his rights under Rule 90(E).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the Prosecution has asked me to give you a -- to inform you about Rule 90(E) -- and it's me, Presiding Judge, who is addressing you at this moment. I'll read Rule 90(E) to you: "A witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber may, however, compel the witness to answer the question. Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." Which means that if you think that a truthful answer to any question Mr. Traldi will put to you - or anyone else - would tend to incriminate yourself, you may address me and ask to be relieved from your duty to answer that question. We'll then consider that. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall at any time in 1992 asking to have your subordinates, including the men I just mentioned, released after they'd been arrested for a crime so that they could be send back to the front?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Is there a document to that effect? I don't remember that I ever requested that. Those men were not members of the brigade which was under Doboj OG. They were probably members of the public security centre in Doboj. I don't remember. If there is a document, could you please show it to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll use a series of documents just so that we get through in some detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's start with 65 ter 32048.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a report on initiating criminal proceedings against members of the military police at the Security Services Centre in Doboj. And problems relating to the actions of judicial organs. You see it's from the office of the public prosecutor in Teslic and addressees include the Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Interior, and the Ministry of National Defence. And we see a reference in the first paragraph to a criminal report, the office of the public prosecutor received against a number of persons, including Slobodan Karagic, and the men that we just discussed. Now, scrolling down to the bottom of the first paragraph, bottom at the page in English, the document says the Office of the Public Prosecutor received a report against them for crimes, including robbery, extortion, aggravated theft, and murder. And if we turn to page 2 in the English, at point 2, we read that on the 10th of July, the Office of the Public Prosecutor in Teslic filed a request to initiate an investigation against these reported persons on the suspicion that they had committed the crimes of illegal arrest, robbery, and extortion, and for some of them, also the crimes of aggravated theft and murder. Are you familiar with this case?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, one second, please. The interpreters have difficulties in hearing you because you your microphone is not adjusted. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This information was written on the 28th of July. I don't know who this was sent to. This information, as far as I can remember, and my memory serves me well, I did not receive this information, and I couldn't have known about this. This was done by the CSB Doboj because they had within their jurisdiction Teslic, the CSB Teslic. They worked on the basis of their laws. I don't know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So it's your evidence you never heard about this case?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: I did not know, no. Now was this sent to my name or the command? I don't know. Does this information contain information about who this was sent to? I cannot see this from this document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness's microphone please be adjusted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you also answer the last question that was put to you by Mr. Traldi. Whether it is your evidence that you never heard about this case, irrespective of whether this was sent to you or not, but did you ever hear about this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 32049.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see here this is headed: "Doboj Operations Group Command, identified as to the Teslic public prosecutor's office, to the Teslic lower court, and subject Dario Slavuljica, request for release." Now, that's one of the men in the document we just looked at. In the first paragraph here, we see he is identified as a soldier, serving compulsory military service as a member of military police. In the second paragraph, we read that: "Based on what we have been told, it may be deduced that Dario Slavuljica acted as a member of the military police unit and that he carried out orders issued by his superior officer who has been charged with the alleged acts." Turning to page 2, we see - and I'll give it a minute for the B/C/S - we see the stamp. That's, again, the stamp of Operation Group Doboj; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And whose name does this document bear?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Whose is it?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is it yours?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Does that refresh your recollection as to whether you were, in fact, familiar with this particular case?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, since I signed it - and that was probably 19 years ago - I was probably aware of it. As for the future fate of this case, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's turn back to the previous page in the English at the bottom, and actually the previous page in the B/C/S as well; also at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read that you write: "We wish to underline that no one has the right to gamble with the destiny of a Serbian fighter who honourably carried out his military duties in the struggle for liberation of Serbian territories from various paramilitary units." Now, taken together with the rest of this document, does that refresh your recollection as to whether Mr. Slavuljica was one of your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: If I remembered, I would know what position he held. If he did hold a position. In the command of the operations group, Slavuljica was not there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Looking at the top paragraph currently on our screen in the English and the paragraph beginning with: "Dana 21.5.1992" in the B/C/S, we read: "His one-year military service term expired on 21 May 1992. In order to serve additional three months, he managed to get across from Mostar to Doboj add midst combat operations and place himself at the disposal of the Serbian Army of BH, under the command of this operations group." Now, it's quite clear that at the time you were saying that Mr. Slavuljica was under your command. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: It's the truth according to the document that he is a soldier. Now where he was deployed which brigade, which battalion, he wasn't at the command, and I was carrying out tasks related to Operation Corridor. If I signed this - and I did sign it - but I do not remember him as a soldier, so I cannot say that's the man, and I cannot say where he was sent and what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32052.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting for that -- In the letter, Mr. Simic, a lot is said about the father of this Mr. Slavuljica. Where did you get that knowledge from, who his father was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To this day, I don't know who his father would be. As for this document here that is stamped and verified, that's not my signature, and I don't know whose signature it is. JUDGE ORIE, Well, I'm referring you to the previous document where you said you did sign it. Which explains the position of the father and I'm addressing you, Witness, I -- explaining the position of his father. Where did you get that knowledge from? Previous document, not this one which is on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whoever it was that wrote the document probably did know, and I signed it, trusting the person who wrote it up. I'm telling you now that I did not know his father. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now we see here this document, again it bears your name in the Operational Group Doboj stamp. It's entitled, "Release of military personnel from detention." And it says: "Your court has ordered an investigation of military personnel from our unit ..." And it lists a number of men, including Ranko Sljuka, Zoran Sljuka, Dario Slavuljica, and some others. We read: "Since the above-named have been questioned, and in view of the fact that extensive combat operations are in progress in the area of Doboj, Teslic and Tesanj municipalities, we request that these members of the military be released immediately in order to take part in these operations." Now does that, again, refresh your recollection as to whether the men I asked you about were members of Operational Group Doboj?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: They are members of the army but members of the operations group or some brigade. I'm looking at this other document. This is not my signature. This is a forged signature. The 17th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see this document bears twice the Operational Group Doboj stamp that you've recognised; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who had access to that stamp?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: The operative organ that kept it in the command of the operations group, but this is obviously a forgery, a forgery of my signature. And, therefore, I am unfamiliar with that concrete situation and this man who is in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's look at 65 ter 32055 quickly. And that will be the last document I show today.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this a ruling from the Teslic lower court dated 21st of July, 1992. And it -- it lists the accused. Many of the names are the same as the ones we have been discussing. And under the word ruling, we read: "Detention is hereby cancelled," and it refers to a number of the accused for whom cancellation of detention was requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 2. Both languages. Under statements of reasons. The English at the bottom. And, I'm sorry, we need to have the very bottom of page one in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see a reference to a letter dated the 17th of July, 1992 from the Doboj operations Group requesting that the men we've been discussing be released immediately, since they were members of the military and were needed to take part in war operations. Now, that refers to the letter we just looked at; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And turning to page 3 now in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S, in the next-to-last paragraph, we read the investigating judge's finding. He notes that: "The majority of the questioned individuals gave statements in which they confessed to the crimes, that the court established that the basis for ordering detention no longer existed, that the court particularly appraised the request put forward by the said military command in the context of time and prevailing circumstances and deduced that following the essential investigation, the accused would be subordinated to the said command and would therefore not be able to impact the criminal proceedings." So basically, the Teslic court is agreeing that these soldiers are needed to fight the war and so they should be released from custody; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJE SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, lest I forget I'd tender three of the four documents on this. Those are 65 ter 32048.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours the number would be P7180.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be P7181.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The numbering would be P7182.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As to the one where the witness didn't recognise his signature, we'll look into it further and I'll -- I may make further submissions. I'm happy to have it marked for identification if the Chamber finds that simplest but I'm in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's appropriate to do because the witness commented on the document so, therefore, it should be on the record somewhere. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 32052 will receive number P7183.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. Witness, we'll adjourn for the day. You may follow the usher but not until after I have instructed you -- one second. One second. Witness. Could the witness put his earphones on again. Mr. Simic, before you leave the courtroom, I instruct you - and it's the Presiding Judge who is addressing you at this moment - I instruct you that -- yes. I instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you have begin today, or whether that's testimony still due to be given tomorrow. If that is clear, we'd like to see you back at 9.30 tomorrow mourning in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood that, and it is clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, before we adjourn ... Yes, we adjourn for the day. Mr. Traldi how much time would you still need tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd be able to be more specific in the morning, I think, but for practical purposes, less than half an hour for my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a look at how much time you used until now. Mr. Lukic, what do you anticipate you would need for re-examination? MR. S. LUKIC: Maybe ten, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 4th of March, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 4th day of March, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.21 p.m.,
